utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Will the registrar call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-04-81-PT, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. May we have the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour, and good afternoon. For the record, I'm Chester Stamp along with Mr. Karim Agha for the Prosecution, and Ms. Skye Winner is our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Counsel, microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: Jim Castle appearing on behalf of Momcilo Perisic, whose appearance has been waived for this proceeding. Also present is Tina Drolec who is our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This is the first Status Conference in respect of the accused Momcilo Perisic. Nonetheless, it raises the same kind of issues that we deal with in Status Conferences, so I'll proceed as quickly and as efficiently as possible. First with pending motions, and I will just go down a list I have and call on the parties as appropriate. The following motions have been filed and are with the Chamber: There is a motion to strike portions of the indictment alleging responsibility for reckless acts, and a motion to strike portions of the indictment alleging responsibility for other inhumane acts. There is also a motion to strike portions of the indictment alleging command responsibility and one for -- in respect of lack of specificity, and the Prosecution has filed a consolidated response for the first two and a separate consolidated response addressing motions three and four. I turn next to disclosure, 66(A)(i), supporting material to the indictment. Mr. Stamp, can you tell us about the state of disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: As far as Rule 66(A)(i) disclosure is concerned that was completed some time ago, and the Prosecution did file a notice of compliance. There was one document accepted, a document which had inadvertently been included in the supporting material although it was a Rule 70 document. The Defence in a cooperative way did waive disclosure of that document for the purposes of time running for Rule 72 application, and we are making efforts to obtain a copy of that document nonetheless to have it disclosed to Defence, and we expect to do so soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Castle.

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: We're satisfied with their efforts, and we're working in a cooperative manner on that issue. We have no objection at this point to the delay of disclosure of that particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And I take it, Mr. Stamp, in respect of the Rule 70 provider you're endeavouring to obtain the consent?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We are obtaining -- endeavouring to obtain --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. We are -- we have made efforts to obtain that consent, and we are also making efforts to obtain a copy of the document from other sources that will allow us to disclose it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. I understand there are 19 witness statements and interviews in the supporting material, although as we will see next, that doesn't represent the totality of the number of witnesses. Mr. Stamp, again, on the number of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm out of practice. Should this case be tried and there's -- and we need to prove by viva voce evidence all the allegations in the indictment, we would probably need to call somewhere in the region of 170 to 200 witnesses, because the case involves three crime bases, two of them being very, very large crime bases and covering a long period -- covering long periods of time, and I speak of the Sarajevo crime base which covers almost two years, a whole city which was the capital of the country, and the Srebrenica crime base which covered a period of months. However, we believe that this is a case which will benefit very much from documents coming in on the basis of adjudicated facts, and also from agreement we have so far had a very cooperative relationship with the Defence, and much of the witness evidence in respect to the crime base, which is a bulk of the evidence in the case, would most likely be material that could be received in evidence under Rule 92 bis. So we believe that as -- that over a period of time the size of the case in terms of time could be narrowed significantly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But any estimate for the Prosecution case?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: At this stage the estimate would be just too vague. I could say eight months, a year, to three years. On one extreme, if we had to prove all of this by viva voce evidence, if there were no adjudicated facts, if there was very little 92 bis, then there would be a significant amount of evidence led for the Prosecution and also for the Defence, but I don't think we will come to that, and I think I could give a much clearer idea of how long this case would last in the forthcoming months. And I suspect it would be a much more abbreviated estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Depending on the progress that is made, at the next Status Conference I may set a deadline for disclosure of Rule 66(A)(ii) statements. Now, Rule 68, that's the mitigating exculpatory material. Your comment on that, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In respect to Rule 68(i) material which we know would fall under the Rule, we're in the process of compiling what would be a significant amount of disclosure in terms of number of documents that we will disclose electronically to the Defence, and we expect to do so before the next Status Conference. In respect to 66(A)(ii), the Defence is aware that most of the material that are available to us is now searchable by them, and the material which is not available for their searches we propose to do the appropriate searches. We have already talked to the Defence asking them to provide us with some guidance as to the areas or the categories that they would consider to be exculpatory material to assist us in focusing Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the searches of those material, and that represents about 20 per cent of material that the OTP has, material which is witness-related material as well as material that comes under Rule 70. So again, we are, for the time being, in a process of cooperating and getting that aspect of the -- of the trial preparation discharged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp. Mr. Castle, on this point and in particular on the guidance being sought as to the criterion for Rule 68 material.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: Our position is we have no objection to providing that guidance. However, it's our position that it's actually the duty of the Prosecutor to make those searches even if we do not provide that guidance, but I will most certainly endeavour to provide that guidance where we can. The problem that is presented when you try to do that is often by providing that guidance you are tipping your hand, so to speak, at the direction of the Defence and so tactically there may be reasons why we cannot do that, but where we can do it I will certainly provide that information to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, you are right, of course, that ultimately the duty's on the Prosecutor under Rule 68, but to the extent that you can, then that would assist the process. Rule 66(B). I understand, Mr. Castle, that you have invoked 66(B).

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: We have, and we'll be following that up with written invocation of 66(B).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thanks. Expert reports under 94 bis. Mr. Stamp, I understand that you anticipate calling 15 expert witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. That was an estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Can you tell us anything more about the reports, the nature of the reports that they will be providing?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There are three crime bases, and there will be expert reports in respect to the commission of the offences, the direct commission of the offences in those crime bases. Sarajevo, if I could give an example, would involve expert reports by persons who can give opinion evidence about sniping and reports by persons who can give opinion evidence about shelling. Then having regard to the casualties, the quantum of the casualties, we would need another expert report for that in Sarajevo, and also, as you can imagine, we would need similar types of reports in respect to the shelling in Zagreb as well as Srebrenica. There are also expert reports which have been commissioned in respect to the allegations covering the chain of the authority of command, the link of the accused to the offences. Two such expert reports have been commissioned, and although I'm not able to advise as to precisely when they'll be ready, I think by the next Status Conference I would be in a better position to give a time when they can be complete. So some reports may be done by one expert. It is possible that one expert may do shelling reports in respect to -- or I shouldn't say shelling reports but may do reports in respect to different matters. So the estimate is about 15 reports. There might be slightly less experts testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see. Yes. Pre-trial preparation. You commented already, Mr. Stamp, on the possibility of utilising Rule 92 bis and 89(F), and I would encourage you to utilise those Rules as much as possible. I'd also encourage both parties to meet to discuss the use of adjudicated facts, agreed facts, and stipulations, and in fact, I will require a report by the next Status Conference on the status of those discussions. The next Status Conference has to be convened on or before Thursday, the 3rd of November, 2005, and I will set Wednesday, the 26th of October as the date of the next Status Conference unless I hear any indications of difficulties. Mr. Castle, your client is on provisional release, so the question of conditions of his detention doesn't arise at this stage. Is there any other matter that any of the parties would wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Nothing from this side, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: Nothing from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, there being no other matter, the hearing is adjourned.
